$comment: Domain summaries, one per guide chapter. A cluster is a human-facing grouping of micro-topics; the graph, not the cluster, is the source of truth for ordering. Colours are chosen to stay legible against both the light and dark page background.

clusters.name: The Messages API, precisely
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: The request shape every call sends, the roles that populate it (including why tool results ride inside a user-role message), the stop_reason values that drive an agentic loop, and the three specific ways a context window degrades under load.
clusters.notesPart: Chapter 1 — Claude API: Fundamentals of Model Interaction

clusters.name: tool_use and schema discipline
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: Why a tool's description — not its name — is what Claude actually chooses between, the three tool_choice modes, and the schema-design rules (nullable fields, 'other'/'unclear' enums) that eliminate syntax errors but leave semantic ones for you to catch.

clusters.name: The agentic loop and hub-and-spoke
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: The loop's only real branch (stop_reason, not parsed text), AgentDefinition's least-privilege allowed_tools, the coordinator/subagent topology with its isolated-context rule, spawning via Task, and the determinism test that decides hook versus prompt.
clusters.notesPart: Chapter 3 — Claude Agent SDK: Building Agentic Systems

clusters.name: MCP: tools, resources, and honest errors
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: MCP's three primitives, project (.mcp.json) versus personal (~/.claude.json) server configuration, and the difference between a structured isError response a coordinator can act on and a generic one it can't.

clusters.name: Configuring Claude Code
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: The three-level CLAUDE.md hierarchy and @path imports, .claude/rules/'s path-scoped loading, commands and skills as the on-demand counterpart to always-loaded CLAUDE.md, planning mode versus direct execution, /compact and /memory, and running headless in CI.
clusters.notesPart: Chapter 5 — Claude Code: Configuration and Workflows

clusters.name: Prompt engineering, made explicit
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: Few-shot examples over vague description, explicit falsifiable criteria in place of 'be conservative,' prompt chaining versus dynamic decomposition, the interview pattern, and validation/retry loops that catch what a schema can't.

clusters.name: The Batches API
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: The 50%-cheaper, up-to-24-hour, no-multi-turn trade-off, custom_id-based partial-failure recovery, and planning a submission window against a real deadline.

clusters.name: Decomposing a task
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: Fixed pipelines for predictable, template-shaped work versus dynamic decomposition for open-ended investigation, worked through with multi-pass code review as the concrete example.

clusters.name: Escalation and human-in-the-loop
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: Which triggers are reliable (an explicit request, a policy gap, a financial threshold) and which aren't (sentiment, self-rated confidence), the three escalation patterns, a self-contained structured handoff, and calibrated confidence routing with stratified auditing.

clusters.name: Error handling across agents
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: The transient/validation/business/permission taxonomy, the four anti-patterns that starve a coordinator of the information it needs, and the structured-error-plus-coverage-annotation shape that replaces them.
clusters.notesPart: Chapter 10 — Error Handling in Multi-agent Systems

clusters.name: Context management in production
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: A facts block that survives summarization, PostToolUse trimming of oversized results, position-aware layout against lost-in-the-middle, scratchpads and subagent delegation to protect the main context, and structured state files for crash recovery.
clusters.notesPart: Chapter 11 — Context Management in Production Systems

clusters.name: Preserving provenance
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: Why a claim without a source, date, and confidence has lost what makes it checkable, preserving conflicting values instead of silently picking one, and rendering by content type once dates resolve an apparent contradiction into a trend.

clusters.name: Claude Code's built-in tools
clusters.subject: Community Guide: Claude Certified Architect
clusters.summary: Matching Glob, Grep, Read, Write, Edit, and Bash to the task at hand, investigating incrementally rather than reading everything up front, and the Read-then-Write fallback for when Edit can't find a unique match.
